column1: ## Features B and C wired into the runner, and the first A-OFF factorial rows. 2026-09-18.
## SMOKE tier, configuration 000/001/010/011 -- the four cells the ablation plan lists as
## `fixed_rank_configurations`, i.e. the ones runnable while `delta` is null and the rank
## selector must refuse. Feature A is refused by `check_preconditions` for exactly that
## reason: BOTH of A's arms need a selector, including the A-OFF silhouette baseline.
## All four cells share arm `matched_budget` with cell_budget 180 and sampling_seed 424242.
## An earlier draft of smoke_001.yaml left C on the full training pool, which would have made
## 000-vs-001 a comparison across two different arms -- C confounded with how many cells each
## side factorized. Corrected before any number below was recorded.
## Rows merged: 134 RESULTS + 8 EXPERIMENTS per configuration. Tracked totals now 1878/72.
## !!!! CORRECTED 2026-09-18, BEFORE THE DEVELOPMENT ROWS WERE READ !!!!
## An audit of the B arm found that all three of B's reported numbers were read in the
## engine's scaled space, which is NOT shared between the two B arms -- and one of them
## REVERSES SIGN in the units that are shared. The original claim, preserved here so the
## correction is legible: "At k=4 outer_0, B improves all three (recov +0.0024,
## uerr -0.1668, loss -0.36)". In count units that loss goes the OTHER WAY, +1.6%.
## The cause, the measurement and the resulting convention are in the B-UNITS section
## below and pre-registered in docs/planning/contracts/B.md. No adoption decision cited
## this file before the correction, and the verdict (INCONCLUSIVE) is unchanged.
## 000 and 001 are IDENTICAL at every rank and fold. That is correct behaviour, not a bug,
## and the runner's own diagnostic says why:
configuration
## C drops a contribution in ONE of twelve cases. It fires when a single optimizer run puts
## two spectra in the same consensus cluster, and at SMOKE the factor bank is only
## `n_iter * k` = 10-20 spectra (5 starts, k <= 4), so a run almost never splits a program.
## The one case that did fire is exactly the one cell where 011 differs from 010
## (outer_0, k=4: recovery 0.7354 -> 0.7353, usage error 0.5578 -> 0.5601). Cause and effect
## line up with no residual, which is the strongest available evidence that the switch is
## wired correctly AND that its absence elsewhere is real rather than a plumbing failure.
## CONSEQUENCE, and it generalises past this run: a 000-vs-001 comparison at SMOKE will
## report "no difference" and that reading would be WRONG. The correct reading is "this tier
## cannot exercise the feature". Feature C requires a factor bank large enough for runs to
## split programs. Measured on the Kang 2018 run (n_iter 10, k 6-14, bank 60-140), C dropped
## 1-9 contributions per rank -- so the capability appears somewhere between these two
## scales, and DEVELOPMENT (n_iter 10, k 4-10, bank 40-100) is the tier to test it at.
## This is the same class of finding the P0-03 feasibility gate exists to catch, now applied
## to a feature rather than to rank selection: asking whether the benchmark is CAPABLE of
## showing the effect before reading a null result as evidence of absence.
## ---- THE RUNTIME GUARD ON C, which is what makes any C number interpretable ----
## `off_path_rel_error_vs_upstream` = 0.0 in all twelve cases: bitwise.
## C modifies the consensus step, which lives in `cnmf.py` and may not be edited, so the
## aggregation is reimplemented harness-side. A reimplementation that silently differed from
## upstream would make every 000-vs-001 contrast measure the divergence rather than the
## feature. The runner therefore recomputes the OFF path on the actual bank at run time and
## REFUSES above 1e-8, rather than trusting the test suite -- the same reasoning as
## `verify_transform_matches_cnmf`, which guards a property of the data, not of the code path.
## Independently pinned in test_features.py against the real Kang banks at k=6,8,10,12,14,
## also at relative Frobenius 0.000e+00.
## `recov` = program_recovery_cosine_v1 (higher better), `uerr` = usage_error_v1 (lower
## better), `loss` = heldout_squared_prediction_error_v1, equal-donor mean (lower better).

## ======== B-UNITS: WHY THE `loss` COLUMN ABOVE MAY NOT BE COMPARED ACROSS B ARMS ========
## Feature B changes which cells reach `cnmf.prepare`, and `prepare` computes its per-gene
## scale `s_g` internally from exactly the cells it receives (cnmf.py:542). So `s_g` is
## DOWNSTREAM of B by construction, and the dictionary, the transform and every scaled-space
## loss live in it. `G` is genuinely frozen across the arms -- verified byte-identical, via
## `prepare(genes_file=...)` -- so the ablation plan's `hold_preprocessing_constant_across_B`
## holds for the gene panel and CANNOT hold for the scale without editing `src/cnmf/**`.
## Measured drift of s_g, B-ON vs B-OFF, outer_0, |G| = 100:
##   mean |log2 ratio| 0.091 (about 6.5% typical); 1 gene of 100 moves more than 20%.
## That is a per-coordinate drift, i.e. a SHEAR, not a rescaling -- the same class of error
## D013 records for the count/scaled confusion. Its measured effect on each endpoint:
##   loss      SIGN OF THE B EFFECT FLIPS IN 4 OF 6 (fold x rank) CELLS
##   recovery  no sign flips; magnitude up to 3.5x different (k=3 outer_0: -0.0019 -> -0.0066)
##   uerr      the Hungarian ALIGNMENT ITSELF differs at k=4 outer_0 (B-OFF 0.7246 -> 0.9846)

## THE CONVENTION, pre-registered in contracts/B.md before these DEVELOPMENT rows were read:
## any quantity compared ACROSS B arms is expressed in COUNT units, because count space is the
## only reference the two arms share. `heldout_squared_prediction_error_counts_v1` is already
## emitted by the runner, so PROTOCOL 5.2's eleven metric names are untouched -- no twelfth
## name was invented to fix this. `heldout_squared_prediction_error_v1` is not withdrawn; it
## remains a valid WITHIN-arm diagnostic.
## The convention does not flatter B: in count units B's predictive error is worse in 4 of 6
## cells where the scaled reading had it improving in 3, while at k=4 outer_0 the count-route
## alignment makes B's usage-error advantage larger. It moves the result in both directions.
## THE SAME TABLE IN COUNT UNITS (`heldout_squared_prediction_error_counts_v1`, equal-donor
## mean, lower better). This is the column a B comparison may read:
candidate_rank
## Note the C signal survives the change of units and is now visible in the loss as well as in
## recovery: at k=4 outer_0 -- the single cell where C fired -- 011 is 1661.5 against 010's
## 1671.5, and 001 equals 000 exactly everywhere, as it must when C never fires.
## WHAT IS NOT FIXED BY THIS. Count-unit reporting removes the artifact from the COMPARISON.
## It does not make the two arms the same estimator: the inference NNLS still solves in each
## arm's own 1/s_g weighting, so two arms with identical programs would still return slightly
## different usages. That residual is arguably part of what B does in deployment, but it is a
## property of the intervention, not something the comparison controls for, and no B result
## may be reported as if it had been controlled.
## A SECOND DEFECT, FOUND BY THE SAME AUDIT AND NOT YET FIXED IN CODE:
## `analysis.assert_poolable` refuses to pool rows spanning more than one `preprocessing_hash`
## and its docstring says such rows "were fitted on different gene panels AND PER-GENE SCALES".
## `preprocessing_hash` contains `s_g_ddof` but NOT `s_g`, so the hash is identical across the
## two B arms -- measured: all four configurations share c9ba55b825846b53205c1816 at outer_0 --
## and the guard would have permitted exactly the pooling its docstring promises to refuse.
## The arms ARE distinguished by `discovery_hash`, which `assert_poolable` does not read.
## Deferred deliberately: changing the hash formula mid-factorial would give one table two
## code definitions. See D016.
## ---- WHAT MAY AND MAY NOT BE CONCLUDED ----
## NO ADOPTION DECISION MAY CITE ANY OF THIS. `smoke_can_promote_feature: false` and
## `allow_scientific_promotion: false`; the ablation plan's margins are all NOT_SET; and
## `contracts/A.md` aside, no feature contract with frozen endpoints exists for B or C.
## scientific_adoption for both B and C is INCONCLUSIVE.
## FEATURE C: untestable at this tier. Not "no effect" -- untestable. Retest at DEVELOPMENT.
## FEATURE B: differences exist but are small and MIXED IN SIGN, and there are two folds.
## READ IN COUNT UNITS, as contracts/B.md now requires: B's predictive error is WORSE at both
## folds for k=2 (+2.7%, +1.4%), worse at outer_0 k=3 and k=4 (+1.2%, +1.6%), and better by a
## third of a percent at outer_1 k=3 and k=4 (-0.3%, -0.3%). Recovery moves by at most 0.007
## and changes sign across folds. With n=2 folds, no sampling replicates, and every difference
## smaller than the 6.5% scale drift the two arms already differ by, nothing here separates a
## B effect from the variance of a single discovery draw -- which is precisely what
## `features.discovery_sample_b`'s fence entry says hardening requires. Reporting the
## direction as a finding would be reading noise; the earlier draft of this file did report a
## direction, from the scaled-space column, and it was the WRONG SIGN in 4 of 6 cells.
## RECOVERY METRIC SANITY: recovery peaks at k=3 = K_true (0.981-0.986) in every configuration
## and both folds, against 0.66 at k=2 and 0.73 at k=4. The metric behaves as P0-04 intended
## on data where the truth is known, which is the first time it has been exercised in the
## runner rather than in tests.
## The matched null for recovery is written to the EXPERIMENTS `notes` field, NOT to a metric
## column: PROTOCOL 5.2 defines exactly eleven metric names and none is a recovery null, and
## inventing a twelfth would break 5.1. It must still travel beside every recovery row --
## measured, K copies of the mean true profile already score ~0.85. Batched into v1.1.
